description: Fig. 6 is a composite of eight low-magnification SEM macro-fractographs of tension-tension fatigue specimens of Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C (wt%) austenitic low-density steel, arranged as two rows of four. The top row (a-d) shows fracture surfaces tested at a stress amplitude of 180 MPa; the bottom row (e-h) at 315 MPa. Within each row, left to right: ST (solution-treated), 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6. Every panel carries a white scale bar labelled 500 μm (bottom right) and a printed area fraction fΔ in the upper-right corner: 180 MPa row, fΔ = 0.53 (a, ST), 0.62 (b, 550-6), 0.74 (c, 600-6), 0.63 (d, 650-6); 315 MPa row, fΔ = 0.25 (e, ST), 0.55 (f, 550-6), 0.43 (g, 600-6), 0.32 (h, 650-6). Yellow dashed curves overlay every surface, delimiting the crack-initiation-plus-propagation zone from the final rapid-fracture zone. Each specimen shows a roughly rectangular gauge cross-section with a rough, fibrous crack-growth region, radial ridge markings fanning from an edge origin, and a smoother, darker overload region. The figure's argument: the dashed-zone area fraction is smallest for ST and largest for 600-6 at 180 MPa and for 550-6 at 315 MPa, matching the ranking of fatigue lives of the aged versus ST conditions.

observations.observation: The figure contains eight SEM macro-fractographs of fatigue fracture surfaces arranged in a 2x4 grid (two rows of four).
Every one of the eight panels carries a white horizontal scale bar labelled "500 μm" at the bottom right.
The printed area fractions in the upper-right corners of the top row read fΔ = 0.53 (a), 0.62 (b), 0.74 (c) and 0.63 (d).
The printed area fractions in the upper-right corners of the bottom row read fΔ = 0.25 (e), 0.55 (f), 0.43 (g) and 0.32 (h).
A yellow dashed curve is drawn across each fracture surface, marking the boundary between the crack-initiation-plus-propagation zone and the remaining fracture area.
Each fracture surface comprises a rough, fibrous region with radial ridge lines fanning from the specimen edge and a smoother, darker region characteristic of final rapid fracture.
The lowest area fraction in the whole figure is fΔ = 0.25 in panel (e) (ST, 315 MPa) and the highest is fΔ = 0.74 in panel (c) (600-6, 180 MPa).
The caption states that panels (a-d) are at a stress amplitude of 180 MPa and panels (e-h) at 315 MPa, for samples ST (a,e), 550-6 (b,f), 600-6 (c,g) and 650-6 (d,h).

All samples exhibit a similar three-zone fracture morphology comprising crack initiation, propagation and rapid fracture regions, with cracks initiating at the surface and propagating radially inward.
At a given stress amplitude the area fraction of the crack initiation and propagation zones is larger in the aged samples than in the ST sample, consistent with their extended fatigue life.
The 600-6 sample showed the largest area fraction at 180 MPa, while the 550-6 sample exhibited the highest at 315 MPa.
The citing text refers to the labelled quantity as fa (area fraction) while the printed annotation on the images uses the symbol fΔ; the two denote the same measurement.

measured_quantities: area fraction of crack initiation and propagation zones, fΔ (dimensionless)
